units.title: Baseline typodont clip

lab.label: Frames with shank visible, dry
Frames with shank visible, spray

units.how:
Record two clips of a bur working on a typodont with your intraoral camera, 30 to 60 seconds each: one dry, one with water spray.
Take 100 evenly spaced frames from each clip.
For each frame, mark yes or no: are both edges of the bur shank visible along at least half its length?
Log the percentage of yes frames for dry and for spray. This is the baseline every later unit has to beat or live with.

units.title: Rigid transforms

lab.label: Max round-trip error of your transform code (T·T⁻¹ on random poses)

units.how:
Write four functions for 3D poses (NumPy is fine): make a pose from R and t, compose two poses, invert a pose, apply a pose to a point.
Generate 1000 random poses: a random rotation axis and angle, and a translation within 50 mm.
For each, compute T times its inverse and apply the result to the point (50, 0, 0) mm. It should come back to (50, 0, 0).
Log the largest distance from (50, 0, 0) over all 1000, in mm. Expect something near 1e-12. Anything above 1e-6 is a bug, most often an inverse that uses minus t instead of minus R-transpose t.

units.title: Camera model and calibration

lab.label: Calibration reprojection RMS

units.how:
Print a small checkerboard that suits the camera's working distance, for example 7 by 5 inner corners with 5 mm squares, and fix it to something flat.
Capture 15 to 20 views: tilt the board, push it into every image corner, and vary the distance.
Run a standard calibration (OpenCV calibrateCamera) with one or two radial distortion coefficients.
Log the RMS reprojection error it reports, in px.
Then calibrate again without three of the views and compute the RMS on those three alone. If it is much worse than the number you logged, take more varied views.

units.title: Synthetic renderer

lab.label: Rendered bur tip vs projected ground truth, max error

units.how:
Write a small renderer that draws the bur (a cylinder with a tip) and the tooth STL from poses you choose, using your calibrated K. Your own projection code or an offscreen renderer both work.
Make the bur tip findable in the image, for example by rendering a one-pixel marker there.
For 20 different poses, project the known 3D tip with K and compare it with where the tip appears in the rendered image.
Log the largest distance, in px. More than about 1 px means a convention is wrong (y up against y down, a half-pixel offset, units), and it must be fixed before any tracker is tested on these renders.
